definitions.explanation: a pen or marker that uses water-soluble ink, as opposed to oil-based or permanent markers

examples.japanese: ホワイトボードには{水性|すいせい}ペンを{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Use a water-based pen for the whiteboard.

examples.japanese: {水性|すいせい}ペンの{汚|よご}れは{水|みず}で{落|お}ちやすい。
examples.english: Water-based pen stains are easy to wash out with water.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}には{服|ふく}についても{洗|あら}える{水性|すいせい}ペンを{持|も}たせるようにしている。
examples.english: I make sure to give the children water-based pens so stains can be washed out of their clothes.

notes:
Combines {水性|すいせい} (water-based) and ペン (pen). A practical stationery term commonly encountered when shopping for office supplies in Japan. Water-based pens are preferred for children and whiteboards because they wash out easily.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水性|すいせい}ペンで{書|か}く: to write with a water-based pen
- {水性|すいせい}ペンのインク: water-based pen ink
- {水性|すいせい}ペンセット: water-based pen set

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {油性|ゆせい}ペン: oil-based pen — permanent marker, does not wash out easily
- マーカー: marker — general term for felt-tip markers
- サインペン: felt-tip pen — a brand-name-derived generic term for fine markers
- {蛍光|けいこう}ペン: highlighter pen
